title: Optimal Finite Interval Discrepancy via Binary Refinement
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz
summary: DeLeo, Henderschedt, and Wells introduced a finite-horizon version of the classical de Bruijn--Erdos interval discrepancy problem. Starting from the unit interval, one repeatedly splits an existing interval into two until $n$ intervals are present, and one minimizes the largest ratio between the longest and shortest intervals over all intermediate partitions. They constructed the lex-merge strategy, whose discrepancy is $2^{1-1/\lceil n/2\rceil}$, and conjectured that this value is optimal for every $n$. We prove the conjecture.
